penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Any Salesforce Flow deployment fix requires deep org-specific access, metadata API knowledge, and hands-on debugging per customer — not automatable by Claude + a prompt.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Diagnosing and fixing deployment pipeline issues in a customer's Salesforce org requires live investigation, screen-sharing, or at minimum back-and-forth async sessions — not self-serve.

rationale: The buyer is real and identifiable — Salesforce admins at SMB-to-enterprise companies who already pay Copado/Gearset rates — and the pain is genuine and recurring. However, the solution space is completely wrong for this factory: fixing Salesforce Flow metadata corruption requires org-specific access and Salesforce metadata API expertise that cannot be packaged as a Claude prompt + landing page. Operational autonomy is near-zero (every fix requires hands-on work in the customer's org), and buildability with Claude's standard tooling is very low. Build gates for operational_autonomy (3 vs. floor of 7) and buildability_with_ai (3 vs. floor of 6) both fail badly, and the weighted total is already below validate threshold before penalties.
solution_plan: This is not buildable as a solo non-technical operator using Claude. The core problem requires Salesforce org access, metadata API manipulation, and deployment pipeline debugging — all of which are per-customer manual work. No Claude prompt or simple landing page can substitute for this. The right players here are Salesforce ISVs (Copado, Gearset) who have dedicated engineering teams and AppExchange distribution. Drop this opportunity.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy gate (3 < 7), buildability_with_ai gate (3 < 6). Total 2.1 is below validate threshold. Drop recommended.
